current_example.title: Example: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations

q-75109.name: Question 1
q-75109.problem: Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
q-75109.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the first row of ${I}_{3}$ and adding $2$ times the third row:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

q-75109.html:
Question 1
?

Consider E=[102010001] and a 3×3 matrix A. Find the row operation that, when applied to A, is equivalent to multiplying A by the given elementary matrix E from the left.

a
R1:=R1+R3
b
R1:=R1+2R2
c
R1:=R1+2R3
d
R1:=2R1
e
R3:=R3+2R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given matrix E is obtained by taking the first row of I3 and adding 2 times the third row:

I=[100010001]R1:=R1+2R3∼[102010001]=E

Therefore, EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R1:=R1+2R3 to A.

q-110463.name: Question 2
q-110463.problem: Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
q-110463.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the third row of ${I}_{3}$ and adding $7$ times the first row:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+7{R}_{1}$ to $A.$

q-32147.name: Question 3
q-32147.problem:
Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$
Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
q-32147.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by swapping the first and the second rows of ${I}_{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary 
row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ to $A.$

q-32147.html:
Question 3
?

Consider E=[010100001] and a 3×3 matrix A. Find the row operation that, when applied to A, is equivalent to multiplying A by the given elementary matrix E from the left.

a
R3:=R3−R2
b
R1↔R3
c
R1:=R1+R2
d
R2:=2R2
e
R1↔R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given matrix E is obtained by swapping the first and the second rows of I3:

I3=[100010001]R1↔R2∼[010100001]=E

Therefore, EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R1↔R2 to A.
q-32147.knowledge_point: Finding the Row Operation Equivalent To Left Multiplication by an Elementary Matrix

q-42537.name: Question 4
q-42537.problem: Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
q-42537.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by taking the first row of ${I}_{3}$ and subtracting the third row:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

q-110462.name: Question 5
q-110462.problem: Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
q-110462.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by multiplying the second row of ${I}_{3}$ by $-\frac{1}{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary 
row operation ${R}_{2}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}$ to $A.$

q-110462.html:
Question 5
?

Consider E=[1000−130001] and a 3×3 matrix A. Find the row operation that, when applied to A, is equivalent to multiplying A by the given elementary matrix E from the left.

a
R2:=−13R2
b
R2:=R2−3R3
c
R2:=R2−13R1
d
R2:=R2+3R1
e
R2:=R2−13R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The given matrix E is obtained by multiplying the second row of I3 by −13:

I3=[100010001]R2:=−13R2∼[1000−130001]=E

Therefore, EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R2:=−13R2 to A.
q-110462.knowledge_point: Finding the Row Operation Equivalent To Left Multiplication by an Elementary Matrix

q-75110.name: Question 6
q-75110.problem:
Suppose that the elementary row operation 
${R}_{1}:=\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-75110.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-75110.html:
Question 6
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R1:=52R1 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
A⋅[5200010001]
b
[5200010001]⋅A
c
A⋅[−5200010001]
d
[−5200010001]⋅A
e
[2500010001]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R1:=52R1 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R1:=52R1∼[5200010001]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA:

[5200010001]⋅A
q-75110.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation

q-110476.name: Question 7
q-110476.problem:
Suppose that the elementary row operation 
${R}_{3}:=\frac{2}{5}{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-110476.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{2}{5}{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{2}{5}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-42534.name: Question 8
q-42534.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-42534.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-42534.html:
Question 8
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R3:=R3−2R1 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100010−201]⋅A
b
[10001000−2]⋅A
c
[10−2010001]⋅A
d
A⋅[10−2010001]
e
A⋅[10001000−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R3:=R3−2R1 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R3:=R3−2R1∼[100010−201]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA: [100010−201]⋅A
q-42534.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation

q-110473.name: Question 9
q-110473.problem:
Suppose that the elementary row operation 
${R}_{1}:=-2{R}_{1}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-110473.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=-2{R}_{1}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Question 9
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R1:=−2R1 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100−210001]⋅A
b
[1−20010001]⋅A
c
[100010−201]⋅A
d
[−200010001]⋅A
e
[10−2010001]⋅A
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R1:=−2R1 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R1:=−2R1∼[−200010001]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA:

[−200010001]⋅A

q-110470.name: Question 10
q-110470.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-110470.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-110470.html:
Question 10
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R1:=R1+2R3 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100010002]⋅A
b
[100210001]⋅A
c
[100010201]⋅A
d
[120010001]⋅A
e
[102010001]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R1:=R1+2R3 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R1:=R1+2R3∼[102010001]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA: [102010001]⋅A
q-110470.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation

q-75162.name: Question 11
q-75162.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}:=-8{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-75162.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The third operation is ${R}_{1}:=-8{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-8{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{3}$ on the left and get ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-75162.html:
Question 11
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R1↔R2,R3:=R3−4R1,R1:=−8R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100010−401]⋅[−800010001]⋅[010100001]⋅A
b
[−800010001]⋅[010100001]⋅[100010−401]⋅A
c
[−800010001]⋅[100010−401]⋅[010100001]⋅A
d
[800010001]⋅[100010401]⋅[010100001]⋅A
e
[−800010001]⋅[100−410001]⋅[010001100]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R1↔R2. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1↔R2∼[010100001]=E1

  • The second operation is R3:=R3−4R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R3:=R3−4R1∼[100010−401]=E2

  • The third operation is R1:=−8R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1:=−8R1∼[−800010001]=E3

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[010100001]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[100010−401]⋅[010100001]⋅A

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to E2E1A, we multiply by E3 on the left and get E3E2E1A:

[−800010001]⋅[100010−401]⋅[010100001]⋅A
q-75162.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations

q-42538.name: Question 12
q-42538.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3},\,{R}_{2}:=-3{R}_{2}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-42538.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{2}:=-3{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-42538.html:
Question 12
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R1:=R1+2R3,R2:=−3R2 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[102010001]⋅[1000−30001]⋅A
b
[100030001]⋅[100010201]⋅A
c
[1000−30001]⋅[102010001]⋅A
d
[1000−30001]⋅[100010201]⋅A
e
[100030001]⋅[102010001]⋅A
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R1:=R1+2R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1:=R1+2R3∼[102010001]=E1

  • The second operation is R2:=−3R2. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R2:=−3R2∼[1000−30001]=E2

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[102010001]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[1000−30001]⋅[102010001]⋅A
q-42538.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations

q-110489.name: Question 13
q-110489.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{3}:=(-1){R}_{3},\,{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-110489.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{3}:=(-1){R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-110489.html:
Question 13
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R3:=(−1)R3,R2↔R3 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100001010]⋅[10001000−1]⋅A
b
[100001010]⋅[10001−1001]⋅A
c
[100001010]⋅[−1000−1000−1]⋅A
d
[100001010]⋅[1000100−11]⋅A
e
[10001000−1]⋅[100001010]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R3:=(−1)R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R3:=(−1)R3∼[10001000−1]=E1

  • The second operation is R2↔R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R2↔R3∼[100001010]=E2

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[10001000−1]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[100001010]⋅[10001000−1]⋅A
q-110489.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations

q-32134.name: Question 14
q-32134.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3},\,{R}_{1}:=3{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-32134.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The third operation is ${R}_{1}:=3{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{3}$ on the left and get ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-32134.html:
Question 14
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R1↔R3,R2:=R2−2R3,R1:=3R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[001010100]⋅[300010001]⋅[10001−2001]⋅A
b
[300010001]⋅[10−2010001]⋅[001010100]⋅A
c
[300010001]⋅[10001−2001]⋅[001010100]⋅A
d
[300010001]⋅[100012001]⋅[001010100]⋅A
e
[300010001]⋅[001010100]⋅[10001−2001]⋅A
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R1↔R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1↔R3∼[001010100]=E1

  • The second operation is R2:=R2−2R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R2:=R2−2R3∼[10001−2001]=E2

  • The third operation is R1:=3R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1:=3R1∼[300010001]=E3

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[001010100]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[10001−2001]⋅[001010100]⋅A

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to E2E1A, we multiply by E3 on the left and get E3E2E1A:

[300010001]⋅[10001−2001]⋅[001010100]⋅A
q-32134.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations

q-32133.name: Question 15
q-32133.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
q-32133.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

q-32133.html:
Question 15
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R1:=R1−2R2,R3:=R3−3R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[1200−10301]⋅[1200−10001]⋅A
b
[1−20010001]⋅[100010−301]⋅A
c
[10−20103−61]⋅[100010−201]⋅A
d
[100010−301]⋅[1−20010001]⋅A
e
[100010301]⋅[120010001]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R1:=R1−2R2. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1:=R1−2R2∼[1−20010001]=E1

  • The second operation is R3:=R3−3R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R3:=R3−3R1∼[100010−301]=E2

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[1−20010001]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[100010−301]⋅[1−20010001]⋅A
